ns2:section.sectionText: This course explores the world of Brazilian cinema from the mid-twentieth century to today. Throughout the semester, we will engage film as a window onto the complex problems of race, gender, and historical memory, as well as the inequalities they produced in Brazilian culture and society. While the first half of the course focuses on cinematic representations of African slavery and Brazil’s colonial past, the second half focuses on the impact of film on contemporary social and political issues in Brazil’s national period. We will learn about different cinematic styles like the chanchada, cinema novo, cinema marginal, the pornochanchada, and the films of the retomada (the so-called restart of Brazilian film in the 1990s) in order to understand the aesthetic and stylistic elements of Brazilian cinema. The course will be TAUGHT IN ENGLISH.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to Graduate - Urbana-Champaign or Undergrad - Urbana-Champaign.
